recipes.name: No Knead Beer Bread
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup warm water (100 degrees F or 38 degrees C)
1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle beer

steps.text: Stir together yeast, 1/2 cup flour and warm water in a large bowl. Cover and let sit in a warm spot for about 30 minutes.

Stir beer, remaining flour and salt into the bowl. Mix until all the flour is incorporated and forms a thick sticky dough that pulls away from the sides of the bowl. Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 2 hours, until doubled in size.
Scrape all the dough from the bowl with a rubber spatula, and place on a well-floured surface. Generously flour the top of the dough and form into a loaf shape.
Sprinkle a baking sheet with cornmeal. Transfer loaf to the baking sheet and sprinkle the top with flour. Cover loosely with a towel and let rise for 30-40 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Place a small loaf pan of warm water on a lower rack to humidify the oven.
Slash a long slit in the top of the loaf with a sharp knife or razor. Place the baking sheet on the rack above the pan of warm water in the oven. Bake for 35 minutes, until the loaf is golden brown.
Transfer to a cooling rack. Let cool completely before slicing and serving.

raw_recipe.headline: No Knead Beer Bread
raw_recipe.description: This really is an easy, fun, and fast recipe, and you'll be amazed at how great the results are, even for the most inexperienced bread maker.

review.reviewBody: This is now my "go to" recipe for homemade white bread. It is super easy and you cannot screw it up. If you have never made bread before, give it a try. You will be surprised by your results! I make the starter in the bowl of my KitchenAid mixer, and let it sit, as stated. Then, using my dough hook attachment, I add the flour and beer and knead for about 3 minutes - until it pulls away from the bowl and looks nice and shiny. Then I let it rise, and after 2 hours or so, punch it down and shape it in my final baking container for the last rise. I use a clay baker with a lid (mason cash cooker), and have found that when I use that, there is no need to put the bowl of water in the oven when I bake it. The clay baker captures the steam and keeps it moist on the inside. I take the lid off for the final 5 minutes to get a super crispy top. I love this recipe!
This was the best bread I've ever tasted! I added some crushed oregano, thyme & basil to dough and wrapped it in rosemary branches while it rose for extra flavor.

Awesome Bread! Easy to make. I let it rise in my dehydrator at 105 for a hour and a half, cutting down prep time. I also added a table spoon of oregano, thyme, and basil, plus a teaspoon of garlic powder, not garlic salt. I went with bread flour and Mich Ultra for the beer. It was all I had in hand. I hope to used a stronger beer next time. The flavor turned out amazing. The fiancé was giving me all kinds of compliments. Thanks for sharing Chef John!

Used Rickard’s Red Ale. The only change I made is that I divided the dough in half and put it in two loaf pans. Very happy with the finished product. Baked it at 425. Used paper loaf liners to ensure the loaves would not stick to the pans. The fresh cooled bread toasts very well. Will definitely make this again. Made it again; baked it in Sassafras bread dome. Did not preheat the dome; buttered the inside and sprinkled with corn meal. Very happy with the result: 8.5 inch diameter, 5 inch high loaf. Baked in 450 oven for 45 minutes with top, then 5 minutes without the top. Internal temp of loaf 198F.

This is one of my absolute favorite bread recipes! I make it with Leffe Blonde Belgian Ale for a wonderful creamy light yellow color and rich flavor. The last time I made it, I divided the dough into 2 round balls for the final rise, then popped each loaf into a small (7 inch round) preheated Dutch oven, snipped each dough ball in 4 places with scissors for decoration, covered each with the Dutch oven lid and baked them in the preheated oven, as directed. Yield: 2 beautiful boules

This is a great simple recipe. I used Voodoo Ranger IPA for the beer. It's a very "hoppie" beer and added a nice flavor. I live 6300 feet above sea level so I reduced the yeast to 3/4tsp, reduced the baking temperature to 425 degrees fahrenheit and baked it in a Dutch oven with the lid on for 20 minutes and uncovered for the last 15 minutes.

Every time I make this - I swear it’s not going to turn out - but it does. I need to start making two because it disappears so fast in our house! Guinness beer is the house favorite. One tip I found by accident is that brushing the bread top with melted butter upon taking it out of the oven will make the crust a bit less crunchy if you’d rather it not so hard. I now cook it in a covered Dutch oven and skip the water step (and cornmeal step) too. We make this regularly now

Love it! Easy, had all the ingredients on hand. I made a couple changes. I added 3 cloves of garlic, reduced the flour just a tad and added 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese. I didn’t top with too much flour, added a couple more tablespoons of Parmesan cheese and brushed with olive oil when I got it out of the oven!

Awesome and stupid easy. I rounded up the salt and yeast to 2 tsp each to bump up the flavor. A stand mixer made mixing much easier. My first loaf stuck bad but parchment paper worked great on my second loaf and made cleanup a breeze.

This was very well liked in our house. I messed up on the first batch because I misread the instructions and added 1 1/2 cups water instead of 1/2 cup. I kept adding flour to balance it out and my husband suggested just tossing it out. But, I ended up using it with 4 mini bread loaf pans.I figured if it was horrible, THEN I'd throw it out. It turned out super! We actually liked this even better than the "correct" version I also made as one loaf. Making it a second time today. Added fresh rosemary the first time. Will omit this time and just try to do the correct recipe! Added to our rotation.

This is a full proof recipe and this is the third time I’ve made it in as many weeks and as a novice bread baker it was great each time. I prefer to bake this bread in a Ditch Oven as I prefer the more rustic look. During last proof, I spray a piece of parchment paper with cooking spray and put the parchment in a large bowl and then place the dough on the parchment paper. When the Dutch Oven is ready, I remove the lid, hold the dough by the parchment paper and place it in the “very-hot” Dutch Oven and bake with the lid on until the last ten minutes and the remove them lid and finish baking. Three times turned out great.
Easy and delicious. Followed the recipe exactly as written. Made it two times today, once using lite beer and another time using stout. Both were good, but the stout gave it more beer flavor.
I added feta cheese and black olives. Great flavour!

I've made this before with consistent results and praise from others. It's been a while, so yesterday, alongside slow cooker roast beef, potatoes and carrots. Instead of a loaf, I made rolls. Like the rookie I am, I timed them to come out right at dinner time. Not at their best because they need time to cool. Still yummy. I put the leftover buns in a bread bag for morning. Wow! It just occurred to me that these have that soft tuggy texture of sourdough and even a similar flavor. More of this in our future for sure.

I’ve made this so many times with different types of beer and I don’t want to say you can’t mess it up but baring your yeast being bad it’s going to come out great every time. Love chef John he’s so encouraging 👩‍🍳
I have made this recipe several times. It is good as is but I have also changed the flours and the different flavors of beer.

Nice easy recipe and end results were great tasting fresh bread. We like that it did not use sugar or butter that you find in other beer bread recipes. We used Dos Equis beer (that’s all we had), next time we may try shiner for a deeper flavor. Fantastic bread and will be using this recipe in the future for sure
Really easy even for a novice like me. Will make again.
